delivered: server/src/wbs.js#scaffoldProject reads the programme's ladder only
requests.measure: Measured on 5.10.0: a programme declared with a six-gate ladder, then a project created under it, carries exactly six gate milestones (Gate A..F, gates 1..6) and no default four.
remaining: An existing project created before its programme declared a ladder can be moved onto that ladder by an explicit, audited act that adopts the milestones already matching and refuses to duplicate the rest. UNTESTED BY RT365: this book was created after the ladder was declared, so the requester has no measurement of this clause either way.
requests.answerToSource: Half of V-8 is already true and was measured again on this round: a project created under a programme that carries a ladder gets exactly that ladder's gates, never both. What you saw is the other half: your sixteen projects were scaffolded BEFORE RBT carried a gate model, and a declared ladder deliberately does not rewrite projects that already exist (D-33.2 — dated gates and filed evidence would move under people's feet). So the gap is the MIGRATION, and it is accepted as such: an explicit act that moves an existing project onto its programme's ladder, adopting the milestones that already match and refusing to duplicate. Until it ships, `adopt` on PUT /api/v1/milestones binds your Gate A..F rows to the scaffolded ones by their predictable ids rather than adding to them.
requests.observed: RESTATED BY THE REQUESTER, and the half RT365 filed as a defect is withdrawn. Round 2 declared the A-F ladder on programme RBT and created sixteen projects into an empty book. Meridian scaffolded exactly one ladder: 96 milestones, six per project, named `Gate A - Discovery` .. `Gate F - Market release`, positions 1..6, with 517 gate criteria and 96 evidence documents derived from the ladder's own evidence strings; `POST /api/criteria {"gate":7}` -> 400 `A criterion belongs to a gate 1..6 of this project's programme`. The delivered half of REQ-27 is therefore confirmed by measurement, not by reading. RBT-GOV nonetheless carries TWELVE milestones, and the cause is entirely RT365's: its loader declares the ladder as `Gate A - Discovery` and then calls `ensure_milestone(gov, f"Gate {g}", ...)`, so the names never match and six plain milestones are added on top of the six scaffolded (scripts/meridian_sync.py:36-43 against :311). Round 1 published this as a Meridian defect; round 2 confirms it is not, and that it got worse - ten milestones in round 1, twelve in round 2, on two different date lines. The genuine remaining request is the migration of a book created before its ladder was declared, and RT365 CANNOT TEST IT: this book was created after. Their own answerToSource already offers `adopt` on `PUT /api/v1/milestones` as the interim (server/src/v1write.js:161-213, 307-310), which RT365 has not adopted.

rt365.note: Restated. The duplication claim is withdrawn as the requester's own defect. Only the migration clause is proposed as remaining, and it is untested by us.

requests.title: Unmeasured is not green: a health state, and honest indices, for a project with nothing to measure
requests.measure: On a book of N budget-less projects with no reported progress, the portfolio tile reads `0 green / 0 amber / 0 red / N not measured`, the health cell reads not measured with its reason, and no schedule or cost index of 1.00 is asserted for those projects on any page, print, export or /api/v1 resource; a project with a budget and reported progress is unchanged; a project whose spend is below the 2 % threshold reads `too early to measure` rather than green.
remaining: A `measurable` guard that treats bac === 0, or no reported progress, as not measurable rather than trivially measurable.
A fourth health state - not measured - counted separately in the ON TRACK tile.
SPI and CPI printed as `-` wherever they are not measured, on every page, export, evidence pack and /api/v1 resource, as the project register row already does correctly.
requests.observed: Measured on an EMPTY book carrying only this programme, in the week two of this programme's Gate B exit documents were refused by their own boards and the gate was not convened. The executive portfolio view reads `PORTFOLIO VALUE $0.00M / 0 funded projects / 16 strategy (no budget) / ON TRACK 100% / 16 green / 0 amber / 0 red / SCHEDULE INDEX 1.00 "at or ahead of plan" / COST INDEX 1.00 "inside the envelope" / FORECAST VARIANCE $0`, and every project row reads `Initiation / GREEN / 0% reported / SPI - / CPI -`. The exported status report goes further and prints a per-project column of `SPI 1.00 / CPI 1.00 / EAC $0.00M`, and the evidence pack for RBT-GOV prints `Health | G - SPI 1.00 and CPI 1.00 both inside tolerance`. The database holds `health: null, pct: null, spi: null, cpi: null, budget: 0` on all sixteen: the colour and the indices are manufactured at read time. The mechanism, in Meridian's own code: shared/engine.js:166-168 `const measurable = pv >= bac * 0.02 && ac >= bac * 0.005;` - with bac = 0 both comparisons are `0 >= 0`, so a zero-budget project is classified measurable, and `const spi = !measurable ? 1 : pv > 0.0001 ? ev / pv : 1;` (same for cpi) yields exactly 1.00; shared/engine.js:190-201 `health()` then returns `{rag:"G", derived:true, why:"SPI 1.00 and CPI 1.00 both inside tolerance"}`. The honest branch exists, is never reached, and is also green: `if (m.measurable === false) return {rag:"G", derived:true, why:"Too early to measure - less than 2% of the plan has been spent"}`. `Engine.roll()` counts these in `green`, which is where ON TRACK 100% comes from, and portfolio.js:333 allows only G|A|R. The same three lines are on the default branch at 5.9.0 (shared/engine.js:128-130), so this is not a branch-only fault. Round 1 saw the same thing diluted to 82% by demonstration data; on an empty book it is 100%.

requests.measure: On a programme with a six-gate ladder, a business case is reconfirmed at gate 6 and a lesson is tagged to gate 5; a gate number outside the programme's declared ladder is refused with a named reason; existing four-gate books are unaffected and the migration alters no stored value.

Source: server/migrations/024_lessons.sql:40 `gate_n integer CHECK (gate_n BETWEEN 1 AND 4)`; server/migrations/028_business_case.sql:52 `reconfirmed_gate integer CHECK (reconfirmed_gate BETWEEN 1 AND 4)`; server/src/routes/portfolio.js:2119, 2163, 2209. Against them, server/migrations/037_gate_criteria.sql:29 is `gate integer NOT NULL CHECK (gate BETWEEN 1 AND 12)` and POST /api/criteria refuses gate 7 with `A criterion belongs to a gate 1..6 of this project's programme` - the ladder is honoured exactly there. Migration 036 freed the ladder; the value and learning objects did not travel with it, and the failure is invisible until a six-gate programme reaches gate 5.

requests.title: Not measured is not within tolerance: a third state in the benefit dimension, and an exception for silence
requests.measure: A project whose benefits are all unmeasured and whose realisation dates have passed raises an exception naming how many benefits are unmeasured and since when; the exception carries its two numbers like every other and closes only by an answer; the benefit tolerance display distinguishes no margin set, nothing measured and within margin as three different statements; a project with no benefits at all is reported by the existing uncased count and raises no duplicate.
remaining: Distinguish within margin, breached and nothing measured in the benefit tolerance and in the sweep.
A benefit past its realise_on with no actual raises its own exception kind, independently of whether a benefit tolerance is set on the project.
requests.observed: Not measured this round - RT365 has no benefit past its realisation date on this book, and no exception could be observed at all: `sweepExceptions()` runs on an hourly setInterval (server/src/index.js:428) with no immediate first pass and no route to trigger it, so a one-day tolerance breached by a four-month slip produced `exceptions: []` inside the session. [Open on RT365's side: leaving an instance running past a sweep tick would settle whether the sweep fires at all on this book.] The code path is unchanged and is cited as read: shared/engine.js:611-627 sets `out.benefit` only when some benefit on the project has an attainment, and attainment (shared/engine.js:646-651) is null unless baseline, target and actual are all present, so `breaches()` returns nothing on that dimension; server/src/exceptions.js returns early for any project with no active tolerance. Measured in passing, and a real constraint on a programme like this one: `Engine.tolerance` needs `bac > 0` for a cost breach (shared/engine.js:585-615), so on a budget-less programme the cost dimension is inert by construction.

requests.title: rollout_wave has a sequence number it forbids you to use
requests.measure: Three waves with different seq values can be recorded against the same project and site and read back in order; existing books with one wave per site are unaffected; if the one-per-site rule is the intended design, the seq column is removed and the 409 message says so.
remaining: Either key the wave by (project_id, site_id, seq), or state in the schema that a wave is one per site and remove the seq column.
requests.observed: Measured. Three waves posted to one project and one site with seq 1, 2 and 3 gave 201, then `409 That record already exists`, then 409. Source: server/migrations/010_plant_and_sites.sql:64-76 `CREATE TABLE rollout_wave (... seq integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, ... UNIQUE (project_id, site_id))`. A project may hold at most one wave per site, so seq can only ever be 1 for that site and the column cannot express what it names. RT365's own rollout is three waves at one site - supervised pilot, then capped autonomous pilot, then controlled market release - and cannot be recorded. One of three intended waves went in.

requests.title: An action can be owned by a body, not only by a person
requests.measure: An action can be created with a body as its owner and appears on that body's agenda; closing it still records a named person; existing person-owned actions are unchanged; a body with no scheduled meeting is reported as such rather than silently unowned.
remaining: An action owner may be a person or a named body; a body-owned action still requires a person to answer it before it can be closed.
requests.observed: Measured. Of 29 open human acts loaded from this programme's ledger, 15 could be given the ledger's own owner and 14 could not, because their stated owner is a body and not a person: Executive Steering, Trading Risk Committee, Compliance & Legal Committee, Finance + Privacy, Finance + Legal, Finance + Broker-Connector, Support & Training Lead, Trading Risk Committee + Exec Steering. `meeting_action.owner_id` is a foreign key to `person` and there is no committee owner. Half of this is RT365's - its ledger names bodies where a tool needs people, and 28 of its 29 open acts carry no due date at all, which is its own finding against itself. The half that is Meridian's is that a governance product which already models a council on a decision record (migrations 034/039) does not let a council own an action.
